author: independent critic pair for python-final-mcq (education reviewer and Python/pytest/psycopg/FastAPI SME reviewer, one model session acting as both roles, plus recorder; did not author the bank), 2026-11-19; education review of all 30 items and the blueprint. Keys for 29 of 30 items executed in a throwaway venv (Python 3.14, pydantic 2.14.4, fastapi 0.165.0, httpx 0.28.1, pytest; q26 and q27 on a real PostgreSQL via a temporary pgserver cluster with psycopg 3; q15 page-grounded). Verdict: approve, 0 critical, 0 high, 0 medium, 3 low.

findings.claim: Both items sit at topic-practice difficulty, not above it. They open the quick-check band (1-9), which the blueprint instructions describe as quicker core checks, so this is acceptable. Keys, distractors and taught scope are sound.

About 2,700 words including code across 30 items (roughly 90 per item; q26, q27, q20, q24, q28 are longest) against 30 minutes. This is tight but plausible for closed-book tracing. The 30 minutes comes from a modelled allowance, not from timing any learner. The repository contract only requires durationMinutes >= item count, which holds.
findings.recommendation: Owner decision on duration, non-blocking; keep 30 as the blueprint instructs.

findings.claim: The stem says 'follows the course guidance on comprehensions', which names the rule that decides the item. The wrong comprehension options are easy to dismiss, so the real discrimination is between the two for-loop options (try inside versus outside the loop), which does test the objective.
